page.layout: One page of verse, one column, centred; running head at top; page number at top left; catchword-like note "Addita" at lower right of text block (a line of the text, not a margin note).

main_text.p:
Non ante plures Actia littora
Videre nautas, quum Pharias potens
Augustus Ægypti cohortes
Viribus imperij reuicit.

Te diua, ditem quaregis Angliam
Seruat benigni gratia Numinis,
Tutela, & aduerfis fidele
Præsidium columénque rebus.

Quòd mœsta, squallens, supplice dextera,
Vultúsque largis fletibus obruens
Cum plebe ieiuna minantem
Damna Deum precibus serenas.

Quid vera possit Religio piis
Armata votis, quid valeant preces,
Testatur Hispani cruore
Purpureum pereuntis æquor.

Disiecta Ponto corpora, nauium
Moles stupenda, gazaque nobilis
Captiua testatur, Ducúmque
Nunc domitus furor impotentum.

His Angla pubes auspiciis valens
Non sustinendo sæuiit impetu,
Classisque deiecit minaces,
Marte pio furiata, fastus,

Vrsitque remis, accipiter velut
Molles columbas, quos fuga certior
Æquor per incertum triumphis
Surripuit properata iustis.

page.notes: Scan is slightly skewed; the final word "Addicta" is printed at lower right, set apart from the verse. Some letters in the long-s and ligature forms are uncertain, notably "Ægypti", "gazaque", "sæuiit" and "columénque", which are transcribed as they appear.
